machine: Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300, CPython 3.12.16 (uv-managed), fastmcp 3.4.5, ezdxf 1.4.4, SQLite 3.53.1

rows.question: With DISCOVERY_MODE=search applied, can a client call a hidden tool directly by name, or does fastmcp refuse it so that every write must go through the call_tool proxy? Are always_visible (pinned) tools both listed and directly callable?
rows.result: Hidden tools remain directly callable. tools/list advertises 3 tools (search_tools, call_tool, describe_tool) yet direct drawing_new, entity_create_line, drawing_info, entity_list and cad_batch all executed; only a non-existent name is refused, with fastmcp's generic 'Not found: Unknown tool'. BaseSearchTransform.get_tool (fastmcp/server/transforms/search/base.py:204-212) catches only the synthetic names and passes every other name to call_next; its docstring (:163) says 'Hidden tools remain callable'. CadSearchTransform.get_tool (discovery/transform.py:277-283) adds only describe_tool. _get_visible_tools (base.py:257-260) only builds the ranked list, it is not a call gate, and pinned tools are left out of the ranked list. With always_visible=[cad_batch, drawing_info, entity_list] tools/list has 6 entries and all are directly callable. Sizes (ratio/v1, chars/4.19): search as shipped 2,108 chars ~503 tokens; search + 3 pinned 11,437 chars ~2,730 tokens; full catalog 374,377 chars ~89,350 tokens. One entity_create_line request is 101 chars direct, 134 via call_tool (+33).
rows.evidence: scratchpad/spikes/s1/probe_s1.py (in-memory fastmcp.Client against server.mcp, AUTOCAD_MCP_BACKEND=ezdxf); key lines: '[search_shipped] direct entity_create_line -> EXECUTED is_error=False', "[search_shipped] direct no_such_tool -> REFUSED ToolError: Not found: Unknown tool: 'no_such_tool'", '[search_pinned3] tools/list n=6', 'proxy overhead chars=33'.
rows.decision: Positive for plan 1.8-11(d): nothing on the server forces writes through the proxy, so the search default can flip without a per-write wrapper cost; the real change is on the client side (hosts offer the model only listed tools), hence the migration note. The plan's 'search + pins <= 1,500 tokens' ceiling is not met by the three proposed pins (2,730, dominated by cad_batch's schema): 1.8-11 must either trim cad_batch's wire schema/description, pin fewer tools, or set the ceiling at the measured value. Not checked: whether a profile-hidden tool (e.g. solid_box with ENABLE_3D off) is still refused on a direct call; 1.8-11 adds that test.

rows.question: Does a stdlib sqlite3 WAL journal (synchronous=NORMAL, busy_timeout=5000) survive the server process being killed (TerminateProcess)? Concurrency, per-record cost, folder effects?
rows.result: 14 kills (8 in the scratchpad, 6 under %LOCALAPPDATA%\autocad-mcp-pro\state-spike) at random 50-500 ms: every logged commit read back (1-34 transactions, 5-170 rows per round), no partial or phantom transaction, parent open 6.9-13.4 ms (median 8.0 / 9.6 ms), first write 0.08-0.24 ms (no stale lock), integrity_check ok 14/14. The -wal/-shm files remain after a kill and the open does not checkpoint (main file stays 4096 B) until wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) or the last connection closes. Two writers: with busy_timeout=5000 the second waited 1,962 ms and succeeded; with 0 it failed at once with sqlite3.OperationalError 'database is locked' (SQLITE_BUSY, 5). Readers during ~100k commits in 2 s: 0 lock errors. Cost of a ~1 KB JSON row: INSERT+COMMIT median 11.1-12.4 us (p95 41-71 us) with NORMAL vs 353-383 us (p95 476-521 us) with FULL (~30x); UPDATE autocommit ~19 us vs ~355-412 us. Folder: same commit cost; under LOCALAPPDATA one first-open outlier of 48.8 ms against a 1.87 ms median (repeat run 0.68 ms median) - consistent with a one-time Defender scan, inferred not proven.
rows.evidence: scratchpad/spikes/s2/s2_probe.py (subcommands kills | concurrency | readers | cost | opens); key lines: 'KILL_SUMMARY ... rounds 8 all_ok True open_ms median 8.01 max 9.37 wal_left 8 shm_left 8', 'CONC busy 5000 ... wait_ms 1961.9', "CONC busy 0 ... 'database is locked' SQLITE_BUSY 5", 'READERS busy 5000 reads 16 errors 0', 'COST NORMAL insert+commit_us median 12.1 p95 48.1', 'COST FULL insert+commit_us median 352.6 p95 488.0'.
rows.decision: For 1.8-03: WAL + synchronous=NORMAL (a process kill loses nothing; only an OS crash or power loss can lose the last commits, which JOURNAL_SYNC=full covers). At open: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and assert the answer is 'wal'; busy_timeout=5000; synchronous=NORMAL; autocommit mode (isolation_level=None) with explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE so a lock upgrade cannot fail with SQLITE_BUSY; sweep rows still 'running' whose owner (pid + start time, stored on the row) is dead to unknown_commit, never rows of a live second server; optionally PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE). No integrity_check on every open (at most quick_check in a diagnostic). SQLITE_BUSY after the 5 s timeout is a journal-write failure recorded as such, never silent. Perf budget: ~12 us per commit (p95 ~70 us) plus ~20 us per state change, i.e. 30-40 us per operation, under 0.1 ms at p95; open once at startup 2-10 ms with ~50 ms outliers. Never FULL (~0.75 ms per operation).

rows.question: Where does the 1.8-17(3) HTTP guard (Origin 403, Host 421, 8 MiB body 413, constant-time token compare, read-only token) plug into fastmcp 3.4.5 and into how server.py starts HTTP?
rows.result: server.py: StaticTokenVerifier built at :543-554 (scopes mcp:read, mcp:write) and passed as FastMCP(auth=_auth) at :560-562; _validate_http_bind :13311, _effective_http_host :13348, _guarded_run_async :13386 wraps mcp.run_async on the instance (:13392) forwarding **kwargs; main() :13395 calls mcp.run() for stdio (:13404) else mcp.run(transport, host, port) (:13406-13411); no http_app( call. fastmcp 3.4.5: http_app(path, middleware: list[ASGIMiddleware], ..., host_origin_protection, allowed_hosts, allowed_origins) (mixins/transport.py:370); run_http_async(..., middleware=None, ...) calls self.http_app(middleware=...) (:328); run()/run_async() pass **transport_kwargs (:75, :109); no custom_middleware. User middleware is appended after the auth middleware (http.py:652-653); the 401 check (RequireAuthMiddleware) sits on the route (:614), so a guard rejects before any auth answer. fastmcp's own HostOriginGuardMiddleware (http.py:225, 421/403) is off by default (settings.py:323) and absent from the SSE app. Observed in-process and under real uvicorn with a pure-ASGI guard: evil Origin 403 (good or bad token), bad Host 421, bad/no token 401, good token initialize 200, Content-Length 9 MiB 413 with receive() called 0 times, tools/list streamed 200 text/event-stream chunked (6 chunks, 243 tools) through the guard. Endpoint path /mcp (settings.py:264). StaticTokenVerifier compares with self.tokens.get(token) (auth/providers/jwt.py:653), not constant-time.
rows.evidence: scratchpad/spikes/s3/probe_guard.py; key lines: "middleware order: ['RequestContextMiddleware', 'AuthenticationMiddleware', 'AuthContextMiddleware', 'Guard']", 'A evil Origin + good token -> 403', 'C bad Host -> 421', 'D bad token -> 401', 'F good token + allowed Origin initialize -> 200', 'I Content-Length 9 MiB -> 413 receive() calls: 0', 'R3 uvicorn tools/list stream -> 200 text/event-stream transfer-encoding: chunked chunks: 6 tools: 243', 'R4 uvicorn 9 MiB body -> 413'.
rows.decision: For 1.8-17(3): wrap mcp.http_app on the instance next to the existing run_async wrap (server.py:13392) so every builder (main(), mcp.run, fastmcp run, http_app()) gets Middleware(HttpGuard) prepended; the guard is pure ASGI (not BaseHTTPMiddleware), rejects on Content-Length and also counts received bytes for chunked bodies; replace StaticTokenVerifier with a small TokenVerifier subclass using hmac.compare_digest, the read-only token being the same verifier issuing an mcp:read-only scope; do not rely on fastmcp's built-in Origin/Host guard (off by default, missing from SSE). Limitation: user middleware runs after AuthenticationMiddleware, so a 403/421/413 does not reveal token validity (harmless). The instance wrap itself was not executed in the spike - same mechanism as the run_async wrap; 1.8-17's test covers it.

rows.question: Live AutoCAD 2026: AcadLWPolyline.Coordinates with a different vertex count; UNDO steps per mech_part_draw; nested StartUndoMark; regen of the *D block after a DIMDEC change (com_backend.py:8248 unmeasured comment); Entity.Update() display; %%c<> override printing a double diameter sign; HATCH loop deletion.
rows.result: Measured on AutoCAD 2026 (25.1s, W.60.0.0) on 2026-11-04 by the live smokes, sub-question by sub-question. (1) Coordinates with a different vertex count: written in place - a 4-vertex LWPOLYLINE set to 6 vertices with two bulges kept its handle (80), its layer and its XDATA, and the points, bulges and perimeter read back exact. (2) UNDO steps per mech_part_draw: unmeasured. (3) Nested StartUndoMark: unmeasured. (4) The *D block after a DIMDEC change: dimstyle_modify DIMDEC 2 -> 0 redrew the linear dimension's block through Update() (rerendered [86], rerender_required false) and the Document.Export read-back shows the new text ('19,6' -> '20'); whether AutoCAD redraws it without that Update() is unmeasured. (5) Entity.Update(): regenerates the *D block - entity_scale's Update() is confirmed by the export read-back (rerendered [86]); on-screen painting was not observed. (6) '%%c<>': prints a double diameter sign - the *D text is 'Ø∅20' (U+00D8 from %%c, then U+2205, the dimension's own prefix). (7) HATCH loop deletion: unmeasured (the verify smoke adds an island loop and reads two loops back; no smoke deletes one). Measured beside it: a SetVariable is an undo record of its own (_UNDO 1 after SetVariable(OSMODE) undid the variable, not the drawing; _REDO after the restore answered 'Nothing to redo').
rows.evidence: live matrix live-fix (scripts/live/run_all.py at 8a74d48, 14/14 pass) edit.json report.s4 {question: 'AcadLWPolyline.Coordinates with a different vertex count', answer: 'in_place'} and report.four_to_six {old: '80', handle: '80', handle_kept: true, points_ok: true, bulges_ok: true, perimeter: 151.111222, perimeter_hand: 151.1112221300699}; the settings smoke rerun at 1eb32d4 (54/54 pass), settings.json report.dimension_truth before {'86': ['19,6', true]}, after {'86': ['20', true]}, modify {changed: {DIMDEC: [2, 0]}, rerendered: ['86'], rerender_required: false}, scale {rerendered: ['86']}, double_prefix_rendered 'Ø∅20', double_prefix_codepoints [U+00D8, U+2205, U+0032, U+0030], checks 'DIMDEC 2 -> 0 redrawn and confirmed by read-back' and 'entity_scale redraws the number (Update + read-back)' pass; the matrix verify.json 'the HATCH reads two loops' (loop_count 2, no deletion); the undo-record measurement: scratch probe on 2026-11-04 ('undo after setvar', 2 entities kept, 'Enter the number of operations to undo...'; 'redo after setvar-restore', 'Nothing to redo') and the matrix space.json 'drawing_redo brings it back, verified' pass after commit e6b5965.
rows.decision: Keep the primary branches: entity_set_vertices writes Coordinates in place (no replace fallback needed on 2026); a dimension's *D block is redrawn with Update() and confirmed by the export read-back (dimstyle_modify, entity_scale, dimension_rerender). dim_double_prefix is confirmed live ('Ø∅20' is printed), so its severity may rise from warning in 1.8.1 as the settings smoke's note plans. UNDO steps per mech_part_draw, nested StartUndoMark and HATCH loop deletion stay unmeasured: their runtime fallbacks stay and no claim is made. _UNDO / _REDO touch no system variable (e6b5965).

rows.question: Which of the three candidate mechanisms reproduces the rival's paper-space circle on 1.7.0 (a DWG saved with Layout1 active + a create; a _SCALE left at the prompt; a corner operation on a paper layout)?
rows.result: Measured on AutoCAD 2026 (25.1s) on 2026-11-04 by scripts/smoke_space_com.py, which reads where 1.7.0's rule (_msp() = ActiveLayout.Block) would have drawn; the 1.7.0 code itself was not run. (a) A DWG saved with Layout1 active and reopened through drawing_open: AutoCAD reopens it on Layout1, so the 1.7.0 rule draws on Layout1 - reproduces. (c) The operator's tab on Layout1 (what a click does) followed by a create or a corner operation: the 1.7.0 rule draws on Layout1 - reproduces; on 1.8.0 every new entity, the trim and the fillet are owned by ModelSpace and no paper layout's Block.Count moves. (b) A _SCALE left at its prompt: not reproduced and not sendable unattended - SendCommand of a command that stops at a prompt does not return until the prompt is answered, PostCommand returns but then every COM call is RPC_E_CALL_REJECTED until a key is pressed in AutoCAD, and ESC characters in a SendCommand string are refused as 'Invalid input'; it leaves the seat blocked rather than drawing in paper space.
rows.evidence: live matrix live-fix (scripts/live/run_all.py at 8a74d48) space.json report.s5 {saved_layout1_then_create: {rule_1_7_draws_on: 'Layout1', reproduces_on_1_7: true}, operator_tab_layout1_then_create: {rule_1_7_draws_on: 'Layout1', reproduces_on_1_7: true}, scale_left_at_prompt: {measured: PROMPT_LIMITATION, note: 'not sent by this smoke'}}; checks 'a DWG saved on Layout1 reopens there and still draws in model space', 'every new entity is owned by ModelSpace', 'no paper layout's Block.Count moved', 'the trim cut the model-space line at the cutter (half of 100 is left)' pass (13/13). The _SCALE measurement: scratch probes on 2026-11-04 (SendCommand blocked until a key press; PostCommand then 'Call was rejected by callee' on CMDACTIVE / LASTPROMPT / SendCommand / Close for 5 s; SendCommand('\u001b\u001b\u001b') -> 'Invalid input').
rows.decision: Both (a) and (c) reproduce on 1.7.0's rule; 1.8-05's bound target space (Model by default, moved only by layout_set_current) fixes both and is kept. (b) is not a paper-space mechanism on this seat but a blocked one: command_incomplete is not reachable through ActiveX on AutoCAD 2026 (the ESC x3 recovery never runs), so a raw command left at its prompt overruns COM_CALL_TIMEOUT; the smoke records this as PROMPT_LIMITATION instead of sending one.
